rows.note: Use this formal medical noun for a fainting or loss-of-consciousness episode.

example.english: The patient suddenly had a collapse, so the doctor arranged an examination immediately.
example.traditional: 病人突然暈厥，醫生即刻安排檢查。
example.jyutping: beng6 jan4 dat6 jin4 wan4 kyut3 ji1 saang1 zik1 hak1 on1 paai4 gim2 caa4

rows.note: Use 塌 for a building, wall, roof, or other rigid structure that caves in or falls down.

example.english: That wall could collapse at any time.
example.jyutping: go2 fuk1 coeng4 ceoi4 si4 wui5 taap3 lok6 lai4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for a soft object deflating or collapsing, and for a plan, business, or operation suddenly failing.

example.english: The shop may collapse before the end of this month.
example.traditional: 間舖頭捱唔過呢個月就會冧。
example.jyutping: gaan1 pou3 tau4 ngaai4 m4 gwo3 ni1 go3 jyut6 zau6 wui5 lam6

rows.note: Use 暈低 when someone passes out and falls because of exhaustion, illness, or a similar cause.

example.english: I will collapse if I keep standing in the sun.
example.traditional: 我再喺太陽底下企落去就會暈低。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zoi3 hai2 taai3 joeng4 dai2 haa6 kei5 lok6 heoi3 zau6 wui5 wan4 dai1

rows.note: Use 摺埋 when something is folded up into a compact form for storage or carrying.

example.english: Collapse the table first; that way it will be easier to carry.
example.traditional: 張枱摺埋先，咁樣先易搬。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 toi2 zip3 maai4 sin1 gam2 joeng6 sin1 ji6 bun1
